rows.vgi.doc_llm: A curated, browsable registry of ready-to-use example HL7 v2 messages, one per row. Query it first to discover what message types this worker handles and to obtain a well-formed sample you can study or copy. Columns: `name` (a short slug id), `message_type` (the HL7 message type such as `ADT^A01` or `ORU^R01`), `trigger_event` (the HL7 trigger-event code such as `A01`), `segment_count` (how many segments the sample has), `description` (a one-line summary), and `message` (the raw, carriage-return-delimited HL7 text). The view takes no arguments and needs no credentials. Note: VGI table functions accept only literal arguments, so paste the `message` text inline into `hl7_segments`, `hl7_fields`, or `hl7_get` rather than passing this column as a subquery.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## example_messages

A small, built-in catalog of sample **HL7 v2** messages you can query without supplying any input. It exists so you can see a well-formed message and the message types this worker understands before calling the parsing functions, which all require a message argument.

Each row describes one sample: a slug `name`, the HL7 `message_type` (e.g. `ADT^A01`, `ORU^R01`), the `trigger_event` code, a precomputed `segment_count`, a short `description`, and the raw CR-delimited `message` text itself. Browse it, sort by `segment_count`, or copy a `message` literal into `hl7_segments`, `hl7_fields`, or `hl7_get` to experiment.

The view is defined over an inline `VALUES` list, so it scans instantly with no network access and no credentials.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT name, message_type, trigger_event, segment_count FROM hl7.main.example_messages ORDER BY segment_count DESC, name;","description":"List the built-in sample messages, richest first, showing their type, trigger event, and segment count."},{"sql":"SELECT strptime(hl7.main.hl7_get(message, 'MSH-7'), '%Y%m%d%H%M%S') AS sent_at, hl7.main.hl7_message_control_id(message) AS control_id, hl7.main.hl7_message_type(message) AS message_type, hl7.main.hl7_version(message) AS version FROM hl7.main.example_messages WHERE hl7.main.is_valid_hl7(message) ORDER BY sent_at, control_id","description":"Turn a table of raw messages into an ordered message log: skip malformed rows with is_valid_hl7, read the send time (MSH-7) with hl7_get as a TIMESTAMP, and add the control id, message type, and version from the MSH accessors (here: MSG00001 ADT^A01 at 12:00, then MSG00002 ORU^R01 at 12:30)."}]
rows.vgi.title: Example HL7 v2 Messages
